Split a file into fixed-size chunks

Source: R/digest_extra.R
chnkfile.Rd

Reads a file as bytes and returns it as consecutive chunks of a fixed size, ready for mrkroot(), mrklvs() and mrkprf(). Use it to pin a large data file as a Merkle root, so that a later change can be traced to the chunk that moved.

Usage

chnkfile(path, chnkbytes = 1048576L)

Arguments

path

Path to an existing file, a single string.

chnkbytes

Chunk size in bytes, a positive whole number (default 1048576, i.e. 1 MiB).

Value

A list of raw vectors, in file order. A zero-length file gives an empty list. Chunks are returned as bytes rather than strings because a file is bytes: an R string cannot hold a zero byte, so a character chunk could not represent an arbitrary binary file at all.

Details

The file is read sequentially with readBin() in pieces of chnkbytes; every chunk has exactly that many bytes except the last, which holds the remainder. All chunks are held in memory at once, so the memory used is about the size of the file. The default 1 MiB chunk is a compromise: smaller chunks localise a change more precisely but make the tree and its proofs larger. An edit that changes the file's length shifts every later chunk boundary, so only edits that keep the length localise to one chunk.

Errors: path that does not name an existing file (or names a directory); chnkbytes that is not a positive whole number.

See also

mrkroot(), sha512file()

Examples

p <- tempfile()
writeLines(rep("some capsule content", 50), p)

# One small chunk size to show the splitting.
ch <- chnkfile(p, chnkbytes = 128)
length(ch)
#> [1] 9
lengths(ch)
#> [1] 128 128 128 128 128 128 128 128  26

# The chunks pin the file as a Merkle root.
mrkroot(ch)
#> [1] "3f565b39becbebbc336618294525d7a1ff45394d68ecaec899d292bb0fd357c1"

# They are the file's bytes, so they concatenate back to it exactly.
identical(unlist(ch), readBin(p, "raw", file.size(p)))
#> [1] TRUE

# Overwriting bytes in place changes exactly one leaf.
b <- readBin(p, "raw", file.size(p))
b[300] <- as.raw(0x58)
q <- tempfile()
writeBin(b, q)
which(mrklvs(ch) != mrklvs(chnkfile(q, chnkbytes = 128)))
#> [1] 3

# a chunk size must be positive
try(chnkfile(p, chnkbytes = 0))
#> Error : chnkfile: `chnkbytes` must be one whole number from 1 to 2147483647
unlink(c(p, q))
